name: Ubykh

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Ubykh (ubyk1235).

notes: Ubykh was a Northwest Caucasian language, extinct since 1992, famous for one of the largest consonant inventories on record (around eighty consonants) over a two- or three-vowel system. It never had a community orthography, so there is no native spelling to convert. What this spec encodes is the Abkhaz-based Cyrillic orthography published as the Wiktionary Ubykh entry guidelines (the "Ubykh (2022)" column of that page's alphabet table), which is the spelling used by every Ubykh headword in the reference gold set. The guidelines page gives an explicit letter-to-IPA table, and this grapheme map reproduces it: secondary articulation is written with trailing modifier letters, so an apostrophe marks pharyngealisation (б' = bˤ, ӷ'ә = ʁˤʷ), ⟨ь⟩ marks palatalisation (гь = ɡʲ, ӄь = qʲ) and ⟨ә⟩ marks labialisation (гә = ɡʷ, шә = ʃʷ). Following Abkhaz Cyrillic practice the plain plosive letters к п т are the EJECTIVES and their descender forms қ ԥ ҭ the aspirates, which is the reverse of the Circassian convention. The four sibilant series are kept apart by letter shape: ш = ʂ against шь = ʃ, ҫ = ɕ, ҽ = ʈʂʰ against ч = tʃʰ. Vowels: ⟨а⟩ = a, ⟨аа⟩ = aː, ⟨ы⟩ = ə; the guidelines page marks ⟨е⟩, ⟨о⟩ and ⟨и⟩ as spellings of the allophones e̞, o̞ and i, and this map takes е = e̞ and о = o̞. The glide letters ⟨и⟩ = j and ⟨у⟩ = w are consonants, so where they carry a syllable of their own the language's default nucleus /ə/ surfaces beside them. The positional rules place that schwa the way the gold writes it: before the glide after a consonant (диа = dəja, зуруԯ = zəwrəwɬ), after it otherwise (Урысшәабла = wərəsʃʷabla, ибадеҭ = jəbade̞tʰ, арнауҭ = arnawətʰ), and not at all when the glide sits between two vowels (ҟауа = qʼawa). ⟨оу⟩ is exempt: ⟨о⟩ already spells the rounded allophone, so the following ⟨у⟩ is a plain coda glide (ӷәоу = ʁʷo̞w). Doubled ⟨оо⟩ is written [o̞ː], parallel to ⟨аа⟩ = aː; the guidelines table lists no long counterpart for the ⟨о⟩ allophone, so that length is taken from the gold transcriptions rather than from the published table. This is a REPRODUCTION of a transcription convention, not a claim about Ubykh as spoken. The orthography is a scholarly one and the gold transcriptions are hand-written, so the residual error is dominated by cases the spelling cannot decide: loanword readings of ⟨г⟩ and ⟨х⟩ as ɡ and x, full-vowel readings of ⟨и⟩ and ⟨у⟩ as i and u, and pharyngealisation written on the vowel rather than on the consonant. Stress exemption: Ubykh word stress is reported as largely predictable (commonly final-syllable) but the primary descriptive sources give no spelling-derivable rule robust enough to encode; no stress block is declared.
